text:
Maya: quick handover before I sign off — active incident still unfolding, handing primary to Rafael. summary: sustained rate-limit errors on /v1/generate for customers in eu-west-1 causing elevated 429 and token retries. alerted via pager at ~15:08 UTC.
Rafael: ack, taking primary. what's the current mitigation state?
Maya: mitigation in progress — automatic fallback routing to `model-small` enabled (50% traffic) and we bumped dedicated pool by +2 nodes via autoscale policy. still seeing bursts; RBAC traffic shaping rules pushed.
Jordan: tagging in — I can watch metrics for anomalous latency during the next hour. which dashboards to watch?
Maya: watch these: <https://console.redwood/instrumentation/dashboards/latency-v1|latency-v1>, <https://console.redwood/instrumentation/alerts|alert-stream>. key metrics: 429 rate, retry_rate_5m, cpu_utilization_gpu_pool, and queue_depth_embeddings.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INC-2026-2045 created by PagerDuty — priority P1 — summary: sustained rate-limit spikes on hosted inference (eu-west-1). responders: Maya (primary), Rafael (next). linked runbook: <https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/rate-limiter-fallback|rate-limiter-fallback-runbook>.
Maya: customer impact: some customers reporting degraded throughput and elevated latency; no data loss. affected: enterprise customers on reserved capacity in eu-west-1 (approx 12 tenants) and a subset of hosted API calls. CS notified with initial template.
Rafael: thanks. any config changes to rollback if this gets worse?
Maya: yes — rollback steps in runbook. quick snippet we used to enable fallback:
```
# enable routing policy override
redwoodctl routing set --region eu-west-1 --route /v1/generate --variant model-small --pct 50 --reason "auto-mitigation"
```
To revert: set --pct 0 or remove override.
Jordan: current alerting: alert group `rl-rate-limit-eu` firing 3/5 rules. I see a short spike in `retry_rate_5m` at 15:25 UTC aligning with a deploy in eu-west-1 earlier today — correlating?
Maya: yes there was a canary earlier, but deploy-checks passed. we left a safety throttle turned off; that might be exposing the pool. current mitigation: re-enable soft-throttle at gateway level. command:
```
# soft throttle at gateway
redwoodctl gateway throttle set --region eu-west-1 --limit 1200rps --soft
```
Rafael: on the exec actions: I'm going to enable throttle and increase pool again if necessary. will also open a followup PD incident if 429 stays >5% for 15m.
Maya: FYI cluster autoscaler is near max for that shard — we might hit capacity. fallback routing buys us time but note quality regressions for some customers. CS message updated to include degradation and timelines.
incident-bot: Deploy bot detected `deploy/ingress-service` at 2026-06-02T14:58Z — linked to incident for context.
deploy-bot: revert available: `deploy revert ingress-service --to 2026-06-02T14:20Z` (requires approvals).
Rafael: I'll send a quick msg to product about potential perf/quality tradeoffs. Jordan, can you keep an eye on `model-small` output quality alerts? we don't want silent regressions.
Jordan: yup watching `eval-regressions` and sample logs. so far quality alert noise is low but we'll run a sample against a saved prompt set every 10m.
Maya: coverage gap to note: APAC oncall is out til tomorrow morning and we have no secondary in that timezone for eu-west-1 late window — if the incident escalates to multi-region, we may need volunteer coverage. Rafael can you coordinate with oncall-schedule for an overlap?
Rafael: will ping @oncall-schedule and see who can cover overnight. also will draft a short status blurb for CS + account reps.
Maya: my checklist before sign-off: 1) updated runbook with exact commands (done) 2) CS templated message (done) 3) set monitoring snapshots for 2h (done). leaving the incident channel to Rafael.
Rafael: confirmed — I'm primary now. actions I'm taking: enable gateway soft-throttle, monitor 10m windows, increase dedicated pool if retry_rate stays >3% for 15m, escalate to infra if autoscaler hits 95%. leaving notes here for next shift.
Jordan: will coordinate log sampling and post any quality regressions in-thread.
Maya: thanks team, logging off in 10. feel free to @mention me if we need escalation. :thumbsup:
Rafael: thanks Maya. team, please add any runbook followups here.
Jordan: adding one TODO: create a small synthetic test that hits fallback route to validate latency/quality after routing changes. I'll add to the runbook after current noise subsides.
Rafael: copying final action items: toggle gateway throttle, maintain fallback at 50% until stable, watch retry and 429 metrics, contact APAC coverage if multi-region escalates, prep PD escalation if 429>5% sustained.
Maya: end of thread.
